species.name: Anaconda
mustRead: massively thick muscular body
eyes and nostrils set high on top of the head
dark oval blotches over olive-green skin
species.note: the heaviest snake - the body must read as thick as a thigh, not as a rope

species.name: Boa
mustRead: saddle-shaped dorsal blotches that redden toward the tail
heavy arrow-shaped head with a dark eye stripe
thick body tapering to a short tail

species.name: Cobra
mustRead: flared hood spread behind the head
front third of the body reared vertically
coiled base with a fixed lidless stare
species.note: the hood is spread ribs, not a collar; the reared cobra is taller than it is wide

species.name: Viper
mustRead: broad triangular head sharply set off from a thin neck
short thick heavy body
zigzag or diamond dorsal chain pattern
species.note: generic representative: a European adder / pit-viper type; the pupils are vertical slits and the coil sits low and flat

species.name: Tree Snake
mustRead: extremely slender whip-thin body
large eyes with a long pointed snout
body draped in loose loops across branches
species.note: generic representative: a vine/green tree snake. The body is startlingly thin - pencil-width even at a metre long

species.name: Rat Snake
mustRead: long slender body with a flat-bottomed loaf cross-section
blunt rounded head barely wider than the neck
large round eyes with round pupils
species.note: generic representative: a black/corn rat snake; a harmless colubrid with no triangular viper head

species.name: Garter Snake
mustRead: long pale stripes running the whole body length
slender limbless body
small head barely wider than the neck

species.name: Cottonmouth
mustRead: thick heavy-bodied build
blocky triangular pit-viper head much wider than the neck
white mouth lining shown in a gape

species.name: Water Snake
mustRead: keeled banded body
narrow head with eyes set high
slender tapering tail

species.name: Mamba
mustRead: very long slender whip-like body
narrow coffin-shaped head
smooth uniform scales with a fixed grin mouthline
species.note: Slim and elongate, not thick like a viper; often drawn rearing with the front third raised.

species.name: Rattlesnake
mustRead: segmented rattle on the tail tip
broad triangular arrow-shaped head on a thin neck
thick body coiled with the neck reared in an S

species.name: Racer
mustRead: very slender whip-thin body in a fast S-curve
smooth glossy uniform scales
large eye on a narrow rounded head
species.note: Name read as the North American racer snake (Coluber), a slim fast-moving colubrid, not a lizard or a 'racerunner'.

species.name: Mountain Viper
mustRead: broad triangular head much wider than the neck
thick stocky body with a zigzag dorsal band
vertical slit pupil

species.name: Whip Snake
mustRead: extremely thin whip-like body
very long tapering tail half the total length
narrow head with a large round eye

species.name: Grass Snake
mustRead: pale yellow collar behind the head
olive-grey body in a loose S-curve
round pupil in a rounded non-triangular head

species.name: Sand Boa
mustRead: thick stubby cylindrical body
blunt wedge snout with tiny upward-facing eyes
very short abruptly blunt tail
species.note: Far shorter and fatter than typical snakes; the tail is a stub, so head and tail ends look almost interchangeable.

species.name: King Snake
mustRead: bold repeating bands or rings of colour around the body
smooth glossy scales
narrow head barely wider than the neck

species.name: Cave Snake
mustRead: limbless coiled rope body
pale washed-out unpigmented scales
blunt wedge head with heat-sensing pits
species.note: Generic name - interpreted as a pale cave-dwelling ratsnake/pitviper type.

species.name: Snake
mustRead: limbless tapering body in S-curves
wedge head continuous with the neck
flicking forked tongue
species.note: Generic name - interpreted as a representative colubrid.

species.name: Caecilian
mustRead: limbless worm-like body ringed with annular grooves
blunt bullet-shaped head with a tiny sensory tentacle
no visible eyes and no tail fin
species.note: An amphibian, not a worm or a snake - the rings are skin folds, and it has slick moist skin with no scales.

species.name: Vine Snake
mustRead: needle-thin whip-like body
long pointed dart-shaped snout
horizontal keyhole-shaped pupils
species.note: Extraordinarily thin - roughly pencil-width along its whole length, not a tapering rope like a typical snake.
